text:
jin: Hey infra — during the Dedicated pool rollout in us-east-1 we're hitting intermittent failures when registering targets behind NLBs through interface VPC endpoints. errors look like 'TargetRegistrationThrottled' in the logs. started ~2024-06-05 16:17 UTC.

anita: I saw that too. traffic spike + parallel rollout caused a bunch of simultaneous target registrations. suspect we're hitting a registration-rate soft limit on the backend.

dave: Can you paste a sample error and the affected account/region? I'll check current quotas.

jin: sample log: `ERROR: TargetRegistrationThrottled: Rate exceeded while registering targets: 50 -> 429` account: 123456789012 region: us-east-1 stacks: redwood-dedicated-nlb-{a,b,c} trying to register ~1200 targets over ~5m during scale-up.

dave: Ok confirmed with the console — our current documented guidance shows a registration rate being throttled at ~100 reqs/s across VPCE->NLB path for this account in us-east-1. There's also a per-target-group soft cap that looks like it's being hit in AZ b. I'll open an AWS case but we should also add mitigations.

anita: Mitigations: 1) stagger target registration with jitter (we already have retries but need backoff tuning) 2) pre-warm target groups in low-traffic window (create placeholder targets then swap) 3) route new Dedicated traffic to alternate region temporarily if capacity exists. Also add exponential backoff to infra agent that registers nodes.

jin: Can we request the following from AWS: increase registration rate to 500 reqs/s and bump targets-per-nlb soft limit from 2k to 6k in us-east-1 for account 123456789012. Also request interface endpoint attach-rate to allow more quick enrollments per AZ.

dave: Filed AWS Support case 9876543210 (service: Elastic Load Balancing). Summary: "Increase NLB target registration rate and targets per NLB (soft) for account 123456789012 in us-east-1". Included sample error logs, deployment window, and justification (dedicated pool rollout, multi-tenant safe, plan for gradual ramp). Case ETA: initial response ~4-12h, request approval may take 24-72h.

ops-bot: Incident note created: INC-20240605-14. Link: https://redwood.ops/incidents/INC-20240605-14

sara: For immediate relief I pushed a temporary rollout pause and reduced parallelism from 50 -> 8 registrations/sec. Rolling back a couple of canaries to reduce churn. Will monitor error rate for 30m and then try gradual ramp.

anita: Also add a queue in the registrar service and drain at safe throughput. I'll open a PR to change default concurrency and add metrics for registration_rps and registration_errors.

jin: Thanks. Once AWS confirms increase, we'll coordinate a controlled ramp and note cost/availability impacts. leaving this thread open — update when case moves or when PR lands. :thumbsup:
